notes.claim: A truss of three members joined at three joints is rigid: it will not greatly deform or collapse under a small load.
In a simple truss the members m and joints j are related by m = 2j - 3.
A member whose force on a pin points toward the pin is in compression; if it points away from the pin, it is in tension.
The mechanical advantage of a screw is its circumference divided by its pitch.

sources.title: Chapter 6 ANALYSIS OF STRUCTURES
sources.quote: A truss is said to be rigid if it is designed in such a way that it will not greatly deform or collapse under a small load. A triangular truss consisting of three members connected at three joints is clearly a rigid truss.

sources.title: Trusses
sources.quote: In a simple truss, m = 2j - 3 # where m is the total number of members and j is the number of joints.

sources.title: Chapter 6 ANALYSIS OF STRUCTURES
sources.quote: If the force exerted by a member on a pin is directed toward that pin, the member is in compression ; if it is directed away from the pin, the member is in tension

sources.title: Mechanical Advantage of Simple Machines | BoxSand – Flip the Classroom
sources.quote: The mechanical advantage of a screw can be found by dividing the circumference of the screw by the pitch (lead) of the screw.
sources.note: i5: a screw's advantage is its circumference ÷ its pitch, so a finer thread lifts more (screens 12 and 13, and the explanation's screw paragraph).
